1.5 Choosing a transport

All three transports serve the same view: the same visible files, timestamps and composed bytes. They differ in what macOS sees.

Disk NFS WebDAV
macOS sees An exFAT disk attached by hdiutil An NFSv3 volume mounted by mount_nfs A WebDAV share
Launcher mounts it Yes Yes No; use diskproxy-server serve
Counts as a disk Yes, e.g. under Disks in Photo Mechanic No No
Writes Optional, through a shadow file Yes, into a session overlay Rejected
Status Ready Experimental Ready

1.5.1 Disk mode

The server generates an exFAT disk image in memory and serves it as one HTTP resource, card.img. macOS attaches it with hdiutil as a raw disk image and reads it with HTTP range requests. The boot region, allocation table and directory entries are generated; file contents are mapped to ranges of the source files and read on demand; unused space reads as zeros. The image never exists as a file.

Timestamps on the disk carry valid UTC offsets, so macOS does not reinterpret them in the current timezone. Names are written in composed Unicode (NFC), the form macOS’s exFAT driver uses for lookups, while source files are still opened by their own spelling.

1.5.2 NFS mode

The server runs an NFSv3 server on localhost and the launcher mounts it with mount_nfs, which needs no administrator rights:

mount_nfs -o vers=3,tcp,port=P,mountport=P,nolocks,soft,intr,timeo=100,retrans=5 \
  127.0.0.1:/ ~/Volumes/LABEL

The server has no lock manager, so nolocks keeps file locking local to the Mac. Every file operation reaches the server by name, which is what makes NFS useful for capturing writes; see Writable views. NFS mode is experimental: see The NFS unmount hang.

1.5.3 WebDAV mode

WebDAV serves the tree as a read-only share. It is useful for tools and applications that work with folders rather than disks:

diskproxy-server serve /path/to/folder --plugin passthrough --mode webdav

The server prints a JSON line with a URL of the form http://127.0.0.1:PORT/TOKEN/; treat the URL as a password. It implements OPTIONS, PROPFIND with depth 0 or 1, GET and HEAD with single byte ranges, and rejects every other method with 403. The transport guide lists the supported properties and limits.
